rootRulingsBPrep.verbatim:
## 2026-10-28 Root rulings on B admission prep (_reports/2026-10-28/prep/b-admission/README.md section 9)

Root acts under the standing instructions ("merge PRs and continue", "Finish step 3 / Full send"). None of these rulings changes fog semantics, S5-02 or the GM role.

- Q1 (G-B1 probe): rerun the 8 fog rows, without a build, on the A2 closure exact-main image at the B freeze. It is cheap, and it binds the probe to the baseline B is admitted on. The prep run (8/8 on the A2M closure image) is the first-contact record.
- Q2 (`/head` digest): accept and disclose. A default build keeps no journal, so `/head` answers 404 `no head`. The digest sentinel and a positive `/head` 200 are unproven on the built image. Turning the journal on would be a config change, which B does not make. This is a known limit in the B local receipt, not a fog-semantics change.
- Q3 (live refusal): accept that the post-admission live refusal (`refuseFogSocket` on delivery) stays proved by the Jest pin `b14FogContainment.test.ts`. A built black box cannot reach it without changing config under a running server. The built image proves the stored-match refusal on every entrance. Disclose this in the admission and local receipts and in the PR body.
- Q4: no RC-B-1 record. The admission adds `ownershipExceptions` (as A2M did) and `registeredSourceLeaves` (the four leaves).
- Q5: confirmed, 34 case ids and `casesMs` 1,800,000.
- Q6: confirmed as a standing rule. If the A2 implementation PR changes `A2_REQUIRED_CASES` or `runA2Cases` relative to the frozen bytes, rerun G-B0 and validate-leaves before the B freeze.
- Q7 (cap margin): trim at the freeze, not later. Step 3 has no PR slack, and 1 line of margin at the 80-line lifecycle bound is too thin. Trim comments and blank lines only in the B cases and runner leaves, with no behaviour change, until option A is at or under 485 at the 80-line bound (at least 15 lines of margin). Then rerun the B node tests, oxfmt and the Q1 probe on the trimmed bytes, and freeze those bytes outside Git as A2 did.

- B freeze (2026-10-28): B leaves trimmed and frozen read-only at _reports/2026-10-28/prep/b-admission/frozen-20261028/scripts/release/ (SHA256SUMS.txt; Root re-hashed all four). Option A is 402 leaf lines, 482 at the 80-line bound (18 lines of margin); literal 579 at the bound, recorded by capException. Copy the frozen files directly; never apply draft/b-leaves.patch, because with core.autocrlf on, Windows git writes CRLF and the bytes change. The same applies to the A2 frozen leaves.

rootRulingMA5StandingRule.verbatim:
## 2026-10-28 Root ruling: A2 mutant MA5 survived (assertion removal, same class as MA1)

Facts: MA5 deletes the journal gap/duplicate assertion (`row.eventCount === row.maxSequence + 1`) after the concurrent round in concurrent-first-sockets. It passed all 4 owned rows on BUILD_ID 1793172695427 (head 2581096fb). The worker correctly found it is not equivalent.

Ruling: same method as MA1.
1. Build one scratch image with a product mutant PA5 that leaves a journal gap or a duplicate sequence for the cfs match during the concurrent round, at the narrowest append seam (for example the sequence assignment in the match journal append path).
   - Scope it to the cfs match and disclose that.
   - Never commit it; restore it byte-exact.
2. Run the unmutated harness. concurrent-first-sockets must fail on "journal has a gap or duplicate".
3. Run the MA5 harness on the same image, without a rebuild. concurrent-first-sockets must pass.
4. Record MA5 as "killed in combination (witness PA5)".

If no single-seam PA5 reaches that named check (for example, the fault fails an earlier check or breaks the build after one scoped retry), do not stop again. Record MA5 as a disclosed, non-equivalent survivor under the R6 precedent and this ruling, add it to CF-A2M-1's combined-mutant follow-up list, and continue to the lifecycle and the PR.

Standing rule for the rest of Step 3 (B included): a survivor that deletes an assertion is handled this way without a new stop. Any other survivor still stops for Root.

- 2026-10-28: the A2 GPT worker (gpt-6.1-sol) failed on the OpenAI cybersecurity content flag during the PA5 pairing. Root moved the rest of PR 9 to Claude Sonnet in the same checkout (t3-4ff0f332), which waits for the still-running PA5 ticket first. Rule: mutation and fault-injection workers run on Claude.

Built-image mutants: BB1 and BB4 killed at named fog checks, BB2 and BB3 (scratch product faults, never committed, restored byte-exact) killed at named checks, BB5 failed with ECONNREFUSED only (not a named check, not counted as a built kill; not a survivor). Disclosed limits: the post-admission live refusal stays a Jest pin (Root Q3); a default build keeps no journal, so the /head digest sentinel and a positive /head 200 are unproven (Root Q2); inherited A2M R6 survivor and CF-A2M-1; CF-A2-1 (co-op teammate unit commands unconstrained until U38); the real mission GM keeps the player viewer role; S5-02 and OQ-M1 stay open. A built black box cannot reach it without changing config under a running server. The built image proves the stored-match refusal on every entrance (socket, metadata, history, head).

Root Q2: a default build keeps no journal, so the host /head answers 404 {error: no head} both before and after an accepted action. The head digest sentinel and a positive /head 200 are unproven on the built image; the fog-off control accepts a digest or exactly that 404, and the fog-on host /head is 403 with the fixed body, so the gate precedes the journal read. The sentinels are the public event ids.

BB5 (restart skipped between the flip and the refusals) failed with connect ECONNREFUSED because the owned server is stopped for the offline flip, so the skipped restart leaves no server rather than a server holding the old config. It is not a named-check kill and is not counted as a built kill (A2 MA2 precedent); it is not a survivor. The flip order cannot be mutated to leave a live server with the old config because the flip fixture requires a stopped PID.

BB2 and BB3 are scratch product faults (fogMatchAdmission.ts: matchLacksRevealProjection never refuses; matchHeadRoute.ts: the head fog gate is skipped). Each was applied only for its own npm run build, never staged or committed, and restored byte-exact (restoredSha256 equals originalSha256). BB1, BB4 and BB5 are mutated copies of the cases leaf committed on detached HEADs and discarded. The scratch builds replaced the .next image, so the registered BUILD_ID run is the one before them; the BB runs used the B rows only on the mutated image (BB2 BUILD_ID 1793183431719, BB3 1793183266751).

No readiness rerun and no stop condition fired in the built run. The configSha256 of the built image differs from the G-B1 probe image (e5b237a2...) while serverSha256 and sourceTreeSha256 are equal; the config hash covers build-specific values.

The frozen leaf copies kept their read-only attribute from the frozen directory; it was cleared (chmod u+w) before the pure-mutant run, whose first invocation failed with EPERM before any mutation. No byte changed; every leaf equals its frozen hash.
The 22 B pure mutants were rerun on the final leaf bytes and each was killed by an assertion failure; the mutated leaf was restored byte-exact after every run.
Release notes (Root, RELEASE-PRODUCER-1, G-B10): the spectate-policy caveat (S5-02), the RC cost of the done-test, and the printed headSha versus rcSha binding. Routed; Root owns that edit.
Contributors: the worker is Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5); the commit Co-Authored-By trailers follow the Root brief (Claude Opus 5.5) and do not identify the worker.
